USER GUIDE

Budget & Forecast Module

End-to-end budget planning, rolling forecasts, and cash visibility — from annual budget to variance alerts, in one workspace.

1. Overview

The Budget & Forecast module plans, tracks and reforecasts spend across every Cost Center and Project. It reads from your existing Budgets, GL Entries, Purchase Orders and Invoices — it never changes your accounting data behind the scenes, so every number reconciles with your books.

Basic terms used throughout this guide

Company

The legal entity you're working in — if you run more than one company in this system, every budget and report is scoped to one Company at a time.

Fiscal Year

Your accounting year, e.g. “2026”. Every Budget, Forecast Revision and report is tied to a specific Fiscal Year.

Cost Center

A department, branch, or team that spend/revenue is tracked against (e.g. “Marketing”, “Riyadh Branch”). Cost Centers can be nested — spend on a sub-department also rolls up into its parent.

Project

An alternative way to track spend/revenue when work is organised by project instead of by department — you budget against either Cost Center or Project, not both at once.

Account

A line in your Chart of Accounts (e.g. “Office Supplies”, “Consulting Revenue”) — the level of detail budgets and forecasts are entered at.

Actual

Real money already posted to your books (an invoice, payment, journal entry, etc.) — as opposed to Budget or Forecast, which are plans.

Budget & forecast lifecycle

Fiscal Year & Masters → Create Budget → Forecast Revision → Submit for Approval → Approved & Active → Monitor Variance

Cash & scenario lifecycle (parallel)

Recurring Cash Commitments → Cash Forecast → Take Snapshot → Forecast vs Actual Reconciliation

Key concepts

Budget

Your approved annual budget per Cost Center or Project, by Account. The baseline everything else compares against.

Forecast Revision

A rolling, month-by-month forecast that can differ from the original Budget as the year progresses. Multiple named versions supported; one can be marked Active.

Budget Scenario

A what-if overlay on a Budget, Rolling Forecast, or Actuals. Never touches the ledger — only feeds comparison reports.

Recurring Cash Commitment

Fixed cash items that never appear as invoices or orders — payroll, rent, loan EMIs, VAT/ZATCA. Used only by Cash Forecast.

Cash Forecast Snapshot

A frozen copy of a Cash Forecast run, saved so accuracy can be checked later against actuals.

Approval Rule

An optional condition (e.g. amount over 500,000 needs CFO approval) layered on top of the normal workflow.

2. Setup Guide

Start here to get your Budget masters in place before forecasting.

How to fill in a field

Every field table below shows a Type tag next to each field. Here's how to enter data for each type:

Field typeHow you enter it
DataA plain text box — click it and type, e.g. a Title or Scenario Name.
LinkClick the field and start typing a few letters; a dropdown of matching existing records appears — click one to select it. Leave it blank and click again to see the full list.
SelectClick the field to open a dropdown of fixed options, then click the one you want. You can't type a custom value.
DateClick the field — a calendar picker opens; click a day to pick it. You can also type the date directly, e.g. 21-09-2026. Example: the Revision Date field on Forecast Revision defaults to today — click it and pick a different day only if you're backdating the record.
Currency / Float / IntClick the field and type the number directly — no currency symbol or commas needed, the form formats it for you.
CheckA checkbox — click once to tick it, click again to untick. No typing.
Small TextA larger free-text box, used for Remarks/Notes/Description — click and type as much as you need.
TableA child table. Click Add Row to insert a new line, then fill each column's cell the same way as its own type above. Click the row number and use the trash icon to delete a row.

Set up masters

  1. Make sure Fiscal Year, Cost Centers and/or Projects are set up as usual.
  2. Create annual Budget records per Cost Center/Project, with a Monthly Distribution if spend isn't even across the year.
  3. Optionally add Recurring Cash Commitment records for payroll, rent, loan payments and VAT/ZATCA settlements — these feed the Cash Forecast automatically.
Tip: from the Budget form, click “Suggest Budget from History” to open the Budget Suggestion report, which proposes next year's budget from historical actuals (Moving Average or Year-on-Year Growth). Use “Create Draft Budgets” there to generate draft Budget records for review.

Data entry: create a Budget record

Go to Budget & Forecast Workspace → Masters → Budget → New (or search “Budget” → New).

FieldTypeWhat to enter
Budget AgainstSelectChoose Cost Center or Project — this decides which of the next two fields you fill in.
CompanyLinkYour company.
Cost Center / ProjectLinkThe specific Cost Center or Project this budget applies to.
Fiscal YearLinkThe year this budget covers, e.g. 2026.
Monthly DistributionLinkOptional. Pick a Monthly Distribution template if spend isn't even across the year (e.g. seasonal); leave blank for an even 1/12th split.
Applicable on Material Request / Purchase Order / Booking Actual ExpensesCheckTick whichever transactions should be checked against this budget.
Action if Annual / Accumulated Monthly Budget ExceededSelectFor each ticked option above, choose Stop, Warn, or Ignore.
Budget AccountsTableClick Add Row for each account: pick the Account (Link) and enter its Budget Amount (Currency) for the year. Repeat for every account you want to budget.
  1. Fill in the fields above.
  2. Click Save.
  3. Click Submit — Budget is a submittable document; only a submitted Budget is read by the reports in this module.

Roles

Accounts Manager — full access System Manager — full access Accounts User — view & report only Auditor — view, report & export

3. Forecasting Guide

Build and maintain a rolling forecast on top of the approved Budget.

Data entry: create a Forecast Revision

Go to Budget & Forecast Workspace → Masters → Forecast Revision → New.

FieldTypeWhat to enter
CompanyLinkYour company.
Fiscal YearLinkThe year this forecast covers.
Budget AgainstSelectChoose Cost Center or Project.
Cost Center / ProjectLinkThe specific dimension this forecast is for.
Forecast VersionDataA free-text label for this forecast, e.g. “Base” or “Q2 Reforecast”. Multiple versions can exist side by side.
Revision DateDateClick the field to open the calendar picker (or type the date directly). Defaults to today; pick an earlier day only if backdating.
StatusSelectStarts at Draft automatically. You move it forward using the workflow buttons/dropdown at the top of the form (Submit for Approval, Approve, Reject, Resubmit) rather than picking a value directly — see “Approval workflow” below.
Is ActiveCheckTick and save once Approved to make this the version other reports use by default for this Company/Fiscal Year/dimension.
Total Forecast AmountCurrency — read-onlyNot something you type — it's the sum of every Forecast Line's amount, recalculated automatically whenever you save.
RemarksSmall TextOptional free text for any context about this revision.
  1. Fill in the fields above and click Save.
  2. Click “Get Accounts from Budget” — this bulk-fills the Forecast Lines (Table) with one row per Account (Link) + Month (Select), each with a Forecast Amount (Currency), so you don't have to type every line by hand.
  3. In the Forecast Lines table, click into each row's Forecast Amount cell and type the updated number; use the Notes (Small Text) cell for context. Total Forecast Amount at the bottom recalculates automatically.
  4. Save. Status starts as Draft.
  5. Move Status to Pending Approval, then have an Accounts Manager set it to Approved (or Reject it back to Draft with corrections).
  6. Once Approved, tick Is Active and save — only an Approved revision can be Active, and only one Active revision is allowed per Company/Fiscal Year/dimension/Forecast Version.

Approval workflow

Draft → Pending Approval → Approved
Pending Approval → Rejected → Resubmit → Draft
If an Approval Rule matches the document (for example, an amount threshold), the approver must also hold the specific role named in that rule — even if they are an Accounts Manager.

Reviewing accuracy

Use Rolling Forecast to see Actual-to-date blended with the remaining forecast, giving a “Latest Full-Year Forecast” compared against the Approved Budget, with variance and variance %.

4. Scenario & Cash Guide

Data entry: create a Budget Scenario

Go to Budget & Forecast Workspace → Masters → Budget Scenario → New.

FieldTypeWhat to enter
Scenario NameDataA unique name, e.g. “Revenue -10% Stress Test”. This becomes the document name.
Company / Fiscal YearLinkSame as any other budget document.
Budget AgainstSelectCost Center or Project.
Base OnSelectWhat the scenario adjusts: Budget, Rolling Forecast, or Actual (Annualised).
Forecast VersionDataOnly shown if Base On = Rolling Forecast — type the forecast version label to layer adjustments on.
DescriptionSmall TextOptional free text explaining the scenario's purpose.
Scenario LinesTableClick Add Row for each adjustment, then fill: Apply To Select (Cost Center + Account / Cost Center / Project + Account / Project / Account / All), the matching Cost Center / Project / Account Link, Adjustment Type Select (Percentage / Fixed Amount / Absolute Override / Delay in Days), Adjustment Value Float, Party Type Select (Delay in Days only), Period Scope Select (Full Year or Specific Month) and Month Select if specific, plus optional Remarks Small Text.
StatusSelectStarts at Draft automatically; moved forward with the workflow buttons (Submit for Approval, Approve, Reject, Archive, Reopen) rather than picked directly.
  1. Fill in the header fields and add one Scenario Line per adjustment, then Save.
  2. Move Status from Draft → Pending Approval; an Accounts Manager then sets it to Approved (or Archived later).
  3. Compare scenarios using Budget Scenario Comparison or Scenario Impact Summary.

Adjustment types

Percentage Fixed Amount Absolute Override Delay in Days

Data entry: create a Recurring Cash Commitment

Go to Budget & Forecast Workspace → Masters → Recurring Cash Commitment → New. Use this for cash items that never appear as an invoice or order — payroll, rent, loan EMIs, VAT/ZATCA settlements.

FieldTypeWhat to enter
TitleDataA unique, descriptive name, e.g. “Monthly Payroll” — this becomes the document name.
CompanyLinkYour company.
Cost CenterLinkOptional.
DirectionSelectIn (inflow) or Out (outflow).
AmountCurrencyThe cash amount per occurrence — type the number directly.
FrequencySelectWeekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, or One-Time.
Start Date / End DateDateClick each field to open the calendar picker and choose a day. Leave End Date blank for open-ended. Ignored if Frequency is One-Time.
Is ActiveCheckTicked by default — click to untick and stop it appearing in Cash Forecast without deleting it.
ConfidenceSelectConfirmed, Probable, or Tentative — shown in Cash Forecast's detail view.
ClassificationSelectOperating, Investing, Financing, or VAT-ZATCA Settlement.
RemarksSmall TextOptional notes.
  1. Fill in the fields above and click Save — this doctype doesn't require submission.
  2. It now appears automatically in every Cash Forecast report run within its date range.

Track cash position

  1. Use Cash Forecast for a rolling cash view (Weekly/Monthly/Quarterly buckets), combining unpaid invoices, unbilled orders, and Recurring Cash Commitments.
  2. Optionally apply a Budget Scenario's Delay in Days lines to see the cash impact of paying suppliers later or collecting from customers sooner.
  3. Click “Take Snapshot” periodically to freeze the current prediction.
  4. Later, run Forecast vs Actual Cash Reconciliation to see how close past snapshots came to what actually happened.
You never fill in a Cash Forecast Snapshot by hand — clicking “Take Snapshot” creates one automatically per period bucket, recording: Snapshot Date (when you took it), Period Start/End and Period Label (which bucket it covers), and the Predicted Opening Position, Inflow, Outflow, Net Movement and Closing Position at that moment. You can open a saved snapshot afterwards to add a Remarks note, but the predicted figures themselves are never recalculated once saved — that's what makes the later comparison fair.

5. Reports Guide

All reports below — plus 7 summary KPI cards and 6 trend charts — are available on the Budget & Forecast Workspace in the Desk sidebar.

How to run any report

  1. Open the Budget & Forecast Workspace and click the report's name under the Reports card (or its colored shortcut card, where shown).
  2. Set the required filters at the top — at minimum Company and Fiscal Year — the report refreshes automatically as you change filters.
  3. Use the report's own filters/checkboxes (listed per report below) to narrow or reshape the view.
  4. Click any inner action button (e.g. “Take Snapshot”, “Create Draft Budgets”) if the report has one — these are called out below.
  5. Use the standard Frappe report toolbar to Export, Print, or add the report as a Workspace shortcut.
ReportUse it to…Steps: filters & actions
Available to Spend See Budget − Actual − Committed, with utilisation % and an at-risk view. Set From/To Fiscal Year, Period, and optionally Dimension Filter/Account. Tick Rollup to Cost Center/Project for one row per dimension, then tick Only At Risk to hide everything except Near Limit/Over Budget rows. Click a Total Actual or Total Committed cell to drill into GL Entries or the Committed Amount report.
Committed Amount See open Purchase Order and Material Request commitments, summarised or in detail. Set Fiscal Year and Commitment Basis (Expected Date or Transaction Date). Tick Include Material Requests to add pending MRs, and Show Details to switch from a summary to a per-voucher list.
Cash Forecast Project inflows/outflows and cumulative cash position over the coming weeks/months. Set From/To Date and Bucket (Weekly/Monthly/Quarterly). Tick Include Overdue/Opening Cash/Orders/Recurring Commitments as needed, and pick Apply What-If Scenario to preview a Budget Scenario's Delay in Days lines. Click “Take Snapshot” to freeze the current buckets (requires Show Details to be off).
Rolling Forecast Blend Actuals with Forecast to get a latest full-year expectation vs Approved Budget. Set Fiscal Year, Period, and Actual Upto (the cut-off between Actual and Forecast). Pick a Forecast Version and, optionally, a second version to compare against. Choose Current Period Basis (Pro-rated Blend / Actual Only / Forecast Only) to control how the in-progress month is treated.
Budget Suggestion Get a data-driven starting budget for next year, and optionally create draft Budgets. Set Target Fiscal Year, History Months (minimum 3; Year-on-Year Growth needs 6+), and Method (Moving Average or YoY Growth %). Review the suggested vs current-year amounts, then click “Create Draft Budgets” to bulk-create draft Budget records — you'll still need to review and submit each one.
Budget Scenario Comparison Compare up to 3 named scenarios line-by-line against their baseline. Set Fiscal Year and Period, then pick up to 3 Scenarios in the Scenario filters. Tick Show Actual YTD to add a reference column.
Scenario Impact Summary See company-level Revenue/COGS/Margin/Cash impact of up to 2 scenarios vs the base case. Set Fiscal Year, pick Scenario 1 and (optionally) Scenario 2, and set the Net Cash Position Horizon (Days) — default 90.
Variance Alerts Spot Cost Centers already overspending their month-to-date pace. Set Fiscal Year and As Of Date (the cut-off used to pace the budget), then optionally narrow by Dimension Filter/Account. Rows in red have already exceeded their accumulated budget pace.
Forecast vs Actual Cash Reconciliation Check how accurate previous Cash Forecast snapshots were. Set As Of Date and tick Latest Snapshot Only to compare just the most recent snapshot per period instead of every snapshot ever taken.
Budget Variance with Commitment Standard Budget Variance Report plus Committed and Available columns. Set From/To Fiscal Year, Period, and Budget Against (Cost Center/Project), then optionally a Dimension Filter. Tick Show Cumulative to accumulate values period over period.

6. Glossary

Plain-language definitions for terms and report columns used across this module.

Report column meanings

ColumnWhat it means
BudgetThe approved annual amount for that Account/Cost Center/Project, from the submitted Budget record (spread across the year by its Monthly Distribution, or evenly if none is set).
ActualReal money already posted to the General Ledger for that Account/Cost Center/Project — invoices, payments, journal entries, etc.
CommittedMoney not yet posted as Actual but already obligated — the unbilled portion of open Purchase Orders, plus pending Material Requests if included. As a PO gets invoiced, its Committed amount shrinks and moves into Actual, so the two never double-count.
AvailableBudget minus Actual minus Committed — what's left to spend without going over budget.
Utilisation %How much of the Budget has been used up: (Actual + Committed) ÷ Budget, as a percentage.
Variance / Variance %The difference between two figures (e.g. Forecast vs Budget, or Predicted vs Actual cash) — in amount, and as a percentage of the baseline. A negative variance usually means spending more or collecting less than planned.
ConfidenceHow sure a Cash Forecast row is: Confirmed (posted invoice or Recurring Cash Commitment), or Probable (unbilled Sales/Purchase Order pipeline that hasn't been invoiced yet).
ClassificationWhat kind of cash movement it is: Operating (day-to-day trade — invoices/orders are always this), Investing, Financing, or VAT-ZATCA Settlement — the last three only come from Recurring Cash Commitment records.

Roles explained

RoleWhat they can do
System ManagerFull access to everything in this module, including configuring Approval Rules.
Accounts ManagerFull access: create/edit records, run every report, and action every workflow step (Submit for Approval, Approve, Reject, Archive, Reopen, Resubmit).
Accounts UserCan view records and run reports, but cannot create, edit, or action workflow steps.
AuditorCan view records, run reports, and export them — read-only, like Accounts User, without print access.

Approval Rule, explained

An Approval Rule adds an extra condition on top of the normal Draft → Approved workflow. For example, your System Manager could set up a rule saying “if a Forecast Revision's Total Forecast Amount is greater than 500,000, it also needs someone with the CFO role to approve it.” If no rule matches a document, only the normal Accounts Manager approval is needed. Approval Rules are configured by a System Manager (Reference Doctype, Fieldname, Operator, Value, Role, Level) and apply automatically — as a day-to-day user, you'll simply notice that some records need an extra approver before they can move to Approved.
